as_told.title: The Space Act lets NASA withhold sensitive findings

plain: A researcher named Maaneli Derakhshani, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, points to the Space Act of 1958, the law passed by Congress that created NASA, the US space agency. He says that law has always tied NASA closely to the Department of Defense, the US military's parent department, and the story holds that it lets the agency withhold information. If true, it would mean what NASA shares with the public can be shaped by military secrecy.
